data.name: Flip
data.detailed_description:
Flip is a a puzzle game for your eyes and your brain. It has a simple and easy to understand mechanic, but the possible combinations on each puzzle will require deep thinking to solve them in the minimum number of moves. Play just to chill out or to exercise your brain.

It contains four puzzle types designed to challenge your perception in different ways:
  • Simple: match the colors in as few moves as possible.
  • Sided: match both colors and orientations.
  • Wired: untangle the puzzle! Follow the cable to find the correct position.
  • Image: reconstruct the image form the broken parts.

Puzzles are solved by matching the correct order for the pieces. Each solved puzzle earns stars, which are used to unlock further levels and puzzle types.



Some puzzles types require you to pay attention not only to the colors and symbols, but also to the orientation of the pieces. Others types will provide different visual clues.



There are 25 Achievements to unlock, you will need to master all puzzles and levels to collect them.

reviews.review:
Flip is a straightforward puzzle game that takes a simple concept and gradually turns it into a more demanding test of observation, spatial awareness, and efficient problem solving. Developed and published by Perro Electrico, it avoids unnecessary complexity and concentrates almost entirely on its puzzles. The result is an accessible experience that can be understood quickly but still offers enough increasingly difficult situations to challenge players who enjoy logical brain teasers.

The central gameplay revolves around manipulating puzzle pieces until the board reaches the correct arrangement. Matching colors is an important part of the process, but simply reaching the solution is not always the most satisfying objective. Players are encouraged to complete puzzles efficiently, making the number of moves important. This creates an optimization element in which an improvised solution may finish a stage, while a carefully planned sequence can produce a much cleaner result. It encourages thinking before acting rather than endlessly flipping pieces through trial and error.

Variety comes from several puzzle styles built around the same basic philosophy. Simple puzzles provide the most approachable interpretation, concentrating primarily on colors and efficient movement. Sided puzzles introduce orientation as another consideration, forcing players to pay attention not only to where a piece belongs but also to which direction it should face. That additional requirement substantially increases the number of possible arrangements and makes careless moves easier to regret.

Wired puzzles shift attention toward connected lines and cables. Instead of concentrating exclusively on color placement, the player must understand how the different connections interact and determine how to untangle the arrangement. Image puzzles offer another change of pace by turning the board into a fragmented picture that needs to be reconstructed. These variations prevent the game from relying exclusively on one type of challenge, even though every mode retains the same minimalist puzzle-oriented identity.

Progression is supported by a star system. Stronger performances provide stars that contribute toward unlocking additional content, so efficiency has value beyond personal satisfaction. This is an effective way of giving players a reason to revisit puzzles that they have already solved. Finishing a stage establishes that the solution has been understood, but improving it can become a separate challenge. Players who enjoy optimization are therefore likely to get more mileage from the game than those interested only in completing every puzzle once.

The visual presentation is intentionally simple and functional. That restraint suits a game where clarity is more important than spectacle. Puzzle pieces, colors, orientations, images, and connections need to remain immediately understandable, and the uncluttered interface generally keeps attention where it belongs. Anyone expecting elaborate environments, detailed characters, cinematic sequences, or a substantial narrative will find little of that here. Flip is interested in being a pure puzzle experience rather than disguising its mechanics behind a larger adventure.

Its achievement system adds another incentive for completion-focused players. With 25 achievements to pursue, there is additional motivation to explore the available challenges thoroughly and demonstrate mastery beyond basic completion. This works particularly well with the game's compact structure because individual puzzles can be tackled during short sessions. At the same time, trying to obtain better results can easily turn a brief session into a longer attempt to discover the most efficient sequence of moves.

The main weakness is that its deliberately narrow focus will not appeal equally to everyone. The fundamental interaction remains centered on manipulating puzzle arrangements, so players who need frequent changes in genre, elaborate progression systems, multiplayer features, or narrative development may find the experience limited. Some puzzles can also become frustrating when the desired arrangement is visible but the correct sequence of moves remains elusive. However, that frustration is also part of the satisfaction when a previously confusing puzzle finally makes sense.

Steam Deck compatibility is a notable advantage. The game is officially Steam Deck Verified, with its core functionality working through the handheld's controls and its interface remaining usable on the smaller display. Controller prompts and general navigation are appropriately supported, while the game can run using settings suitable for the device. Its viewpoint and methodical pacing also translate naturally to portable play, although demanding visual settings can still make sensible performance adjustments worthwhile for players prioritizing battery life or consistent performance.

Overall, Flip succeeds by developing several forms of logical challenge from a deliberately uncomplicated foundation. Its combination of color arrangements, directional pieces, interconnected wires, image reconstruction, star-based progression, and achievement hunting gives it more substance than its minimalist appearance initially suggests. It is best suited to players who appreciate compact puzzle games where improving a solution can be just as rewarding as discovering it in the first place. The presentation is modest and the scope is narrow, but the underlying puzzle design provides a satisfying mental workout without requiring a major time commitment.

Rating: 8/10
